questions.prompt: How do you usually prepare for exams?
questions.sampleA1: I read. I read book. For exam.
questions.sampleA2: I read my book for the exam. And I do exercises. But sometimes I watch TV because it is boring.
questions.sampleB1: Well, usually I try to study a little bit every day. I think it's better than studying a lot the night before. For example, I make notes and then I read them again. However, sometimes I forget to study!
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I tend to space things out rather than leaving everything till the last minute. I draw up a study plan a week or so before, then I go over my notes bit by bit. I suppose past papers help the most, because they put me at ease about the format.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men o'qiyman. Men kitob o'qiyman. Imtihon uchun.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men imtihonga kitobimni o'qiyman. Va mashqlar qilaman. Lekin ba'zida televizor ko'raman, chunki zerikarli bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, odatda men har kuni ozgina o'qishga harakat qilaman. O'ylashimcha, imtihon oldidan bir kechada ko'p o'qigandan ko'ra shunday qilgan yaxshiroq.
Masalan, men qaydlar qilaman va keyin ularni yana o'qiyman.
Biroq, ba'zida o'qishni unutib qo'yaman!
questions.uzSampleB2:
Mening imtihonga tayyorgarligim odatda ko'p qirrali yondashuvni o'z ichiga oladi.
Avvalo, men shunchaki faktlarni yodlashdan ko'ra, asosiy tushunchalarni tushunishga harakat qilaman. Shuningdek, turli mavzular o'rtasidagi bog'liqlikni vizualizatsiya qilish uchun aqliy xaritalarni yaratish foydali ekanligini aniqladim.
Bundan tashqari, imtihon formatini his qilish va qiyinchiliklarga duch kelishi mumkin bo'lgan har qanday sohalarni aniqlash uchun doimo amaliy savollarga javob berishga harakat qilaman. Bu mening harakatlarimni yanada samaraliroq yo'naltirishga yordam beradi.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - How do you usually prepare for exams?
idioms: by failing to prepare, you are preparing to fail - "tayyorgarlik ko'rmaslik orqali mag'lubiyatga tayyorgarlik ko'rasiz"
phrases: cram at the last minute - "so'nggi daqiqada yodlash"
sentenceStarters: "When it comes to exam preparation, I usually…" - "Imtihonga tayyorgarlik haqida gap ketganda, men odatda…"
"I also find it highly effective to…" - "Men … ni ham juda samarali deb bilaman"

questions.sampleAnswer:
When it comes to exam preparation, I usually start by creating a detailed study schedule a few weeks in advance. This helps me break down the material into manageable chunks instead of cramming at the last minute.
I also find it highly effective to practice with past papers and explain the concepts to a friend. Overall, consistency is key for me, because as they say, "by failing to prepare, you are preparing to fail."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Imtihonga tayyorgarlik ko'rish haqida gap ketganda, odatda bir necha hafta oldin batafsil o'quv jadvalini tuzishdan boshlayman. Bu menga materialni oxirgi daqiqada tiqishtirish o'rniga, uni boshqarish mumkin bo'lgan qismlarga bo'lishga yordam beradi.

Shuningdek, o'tgan imtihon varaqalari bilan mashq qilish va tushunchalarni do'stimga tushuntirishni juda samarali deb bilaman. Umuman olganda, men uchun izchillik muhim, chunki ular aytganidek, "tayyorgarlik ko'rmaslik orqali siz muvaffaqiyatsizlikka tayyorlanasiz".

questions.prompt: Have you ever joined a sports team?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I play football. I like it.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I have. I played football at school. It was fun. We played games and I liked running. But I wasn't very good.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I have joined a sports team. I was on the basketball team in high school. We practiced a lot after school. I think it was a good experience because I learned how to work with other people. However, we didn't win many games.
questions.sampleB2: Yes, actually I have — back in my school days I signed up for the volleyball team. To be honest, I was never the most gifted player, but I loved it. We'd train twice a week, and I quickly learned how to pull my weight. The thing is, being part of a squad taught me to get along with people and it brought us together.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men qatnashganman. Men maktabda futbol o'ynaganman. Qiziqarli edi. Biz o'yinlar o'ynardik va menga yugurish yoqardi. Lekin men unchalik yaxshi emasdim.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men sport jamoasiga qo'shilganman. Men o'rta maktabda basketbol jamoasida edim. Biz darsdan keyin ko'p mashq qilardik. Menimcha, bu yaxshi tajriba edi, chunki men boshqa odamlar bilan qanday ishlashni o'rgandim.
Ammo, biz ko'p o'yinlarda g'alaba qozonmadik.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ha, men bir marta sport jamoasiga qo'shilganman. Universitetda o'qigan paytlarimda, qisqa muddatga eshkak eshish klubining a'zosi bo'lganman. Bu jismonan juda talabchan edi va erta tongdagi mashg'ulotlar juda og'ir edi. Garchi men u bilan uzoq vaqt qolmagan bo'lsam ham, bu menga o'sha darajada raqobatlashish uchun zarur bo'lgan fidoyilik va sadoqatni chin dildan qadrlashni o'rgatdi. Men shuningdek, jamoada ishlash va o'zimni his qilgan chegaralarimdan tashqariga chiqish haqida ko'p narsalarni o'rgandim.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Have you ever joined a sports team?
idioms: a chain is only as strong as its weakest link - "zanjir uning eng zaif halqasichalik kuchli (jamoa hammaga bog'liq)"
be a team player - "jamoa uchun qayg'uradigan odam bo'lmoq"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I certainly have. During high school, I was…" - "Ha, albatta. O'rta maktabda men…"
"Being on that team taught me invaluable lessons about…" - "O'sha jamoada bo'lish menga … haqida bebaho saboqlar berdi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I certainly have. During high school, I was part of the local volleyball team. We practiced twice a week and occasionally competed in regional tournaments, which was incredibly exciting.
Being on that team taught me invaluable lessons about collaboration and discipline. It really showed me the importance of pulling your weight and supporting others, because in a team, "a chain is only as strong as its weakest link."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, albatta. O'rta maktabda o'qigan paytlarimda mahalliy voleybol jamoasining a'zosi edim. Haftada ikki marta mashq qilardik va vaqti-vaqti bilan mintaqaviy turnirlarda qatnashardik, bu juda hayajonli edi.

O'sha jamoada bo'lish menga hamkorlik va intizom haqida bebaho saboqlar berdi. Bu menga o'z hissangni qo'shish va boshqalarni qo'llab-quvvatlashning muhimligini ko'rsatdi, chunki jamoada "zanjir faqat eng zaif halqasi kabi kuchli bo'ladi".

questions.prompt: How do you usually spend your evenings?
questions.sampleA1: I eat dinner. I watch TV. I sleep.
questions.sampleA2: I come home from work and I eat dinner. After dinner, I watch TV or talk to my family. Sometimes I read a book, but I am usually tired.
questions.sampleB1: Usually, I spend my evenings relaxing. After work, I have dinner and then I often watch some TV. Sometimes I meet up with friends, for example, to go to the cinema. I think it's important to relax in the evening before the next day.
questions.sampleB2: Well, to be honest my evenings are pretty low-key. Once I've knocked off work, I like to wind down with a cup of tea and a good series. I suppose I'm not one for going out much on weeknights — I'd rather put my feet up at home. Now and then I'll ring a friend to catch up, but mostly I just recharge my batteries.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men kechki ovqat yeyman. Men televizor ko'raman. Men uxlayman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men ishdan uyga kelaman va kechki ovqat yeyman. Kechki ovqatdan keyin televizor ko'raman yoki oilam bilan gaplashaman. Ba'zan kitob o'qiyman, lekin odatda charchagan bo'laman.
questions.uzSampleB1: Odatda, men kechqurunlarimni dam olish bilan o'tkazaman. Ishdan keyin, kechki ovqatni yeyman va keyin ko'pincha televizor ko'raman. Ba'zan do'stlarim bilan uchrashaman, masalan, kinoga borish uchun. Menimcha, ertangi kundan oldin kechqurun dam olish muhim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Odatda, kechalarim juda sokin o'tadi. Ishdan bo'shaganimdan so'ng, kechki ovqat tayyorlashni va dam olishni yaxshi ko'raman. Kayfiyatimga qarab, hujjatli film ko'rishim yoki kitob o'qishim mumkin. Ba'zida do'stlarim bilan ichimlik ichish uchun uchrashaman yoki sport zaliga boraman. Dam olish va keyingi kunga tayyorgarlik ko'rish uchun tinchlantiruvchi kechki odatim bo'lishi juda muhim deb bilaman.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - How do you usually spend your evenings?
idioms: call it a day - "ishni yakunlamoq (shu kunga yetadi deyish)"
put one's feet up - "oyoqni uzatib dam olmoq"
early to bed, early to rise - "erta yotib, erta turish"
sentenceStarters: "My evenings are usually quite relaxed and quiet…" - "Mening kechqurunlarim odatda juda tinch va osoyishta…"
"After finishing work or studies, I like to…" - "Ish yoki o'qishni tugatgandan so'ng, men … qilishni yoqtiraman"

questions.sampleAnswer:
My evenings are usually quite relaxed and quiet. After finishing work or studies, I like to wind down by reading a few chapters of a novel or catching up on the latest news.
If I have some free time, I often call my friends or family members to see how their day went. Overall, I use my evenings to recharge my batteries so I can be ready and fresh for the next day.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Odatda, kechalarim juda xotirjam va tinch o'tadi. Ish yoki o'qishni tugatgandan so'ng, bir necha bob roman o'qib yoki so'nggi yangiliklardan xabardor bo'lib, dam olishni yoqtiraman.

Agar bo'sh vaqtim bo'lsa, ko'pincha do'stlarim yoki oila a'zolarimga qo'ng'iroq qilib, ularning kuni qanday o'tganini so'rayman. Umuman olganda, kechalarimdan kuch yig'ish uchun foydalanaman, shunda keyingi kunga tayyor va tetik bo'lishim mumkin.

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1: I see a book. And I see a phone.
questions.sampleA2: I see a book and a phone. The phone is new, but the book is old. I like the phone because it's easy.
questions.sampleB1: In the pictures, I see two ways to find words. One is with a book, a dictionary. The other is with a phone, maybe an online dictionary. I think the phone is faster, but the book is good for learning too.
questions.sampleB2: Both pictures depict students studying in a library. In the first, three young people are gathered around a laptop, likely looking up information or collaborating. One girl points at the screen, highlighting a collaborative effort using modern technology. The second picture, in contrast, shows a more traditional study scene. Four students are poring over large physical books, intently taking notes. Essentially, the key difference is their study method: digital versus print. While both portray focused learning, the first suggests teamwork, the second individual academic work.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men kitobni ko'ryapman. Va men telefonni ko'ryapman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men kitob va telefonni ko'ryapman. Telefon yangi, lekin kitob eski. Menga telefon yoqadi, chunki u oson.
questions.uzSampleB1: Rasmlarda men so'zlarni topishning ikki yo'lini ko'ryapman. Biri kitob bilan, lug'at. Ikkinchisi telefon bilan, balki onlayn lug'at. Menimcha, telefon tezroq, lekin kitob ham o'rganish uchun yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Rasmlarda so'zlarni qidirishning ikki xil yondashuvi ko'rsatilgan. Birinchi rasmda smartfon yoki planshetdagi raqamli lug'atdan foydalanayotgan odam tasvirlangan. Ikkinchi rasmda esa an'anaviy, jismoniy lug'atdan foydalanayotgan odam ko'rsatilgan. Raqamli variant tezlik va qulaylikni taklif qilsa, jismoniy lug'at yanada chuqur va keng qamrovli o'rganish tajribasini taqdim etishi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: move with the times - "zamon bilan hamqadam bo'lmoq"
a blast from the past - "o'tmishdan bir shabada (eski narsa)"
sentenceStarters: "In the first picture, I can see someone using…" - "Birinchi rasmda men kimgadir … dan foydalanayotganini ko'ryapman"
"The contrast between the two images illustrates…" - "Ikki rasm orasidagi farq … ni ko'rsatadi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
In the first picture, I can see someone using an online dictionary on a digital device. It looks highly convenient and efficient, as they can instantly search for meanings, pronunciations, and synonyms with just a few taps.
In the second picture, a person is looking up words in a traditional paper dictionary. They are physically flipping through the pages to find what they need. The contrast between the two images perfectly illustrates the shift from traditional study methods to modern digital solutions.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasmda men kimningdir raqamli qurilmada onlayn lug'atdan foydalanayotganini ko'rishim mumkin. Bu juda qulay va samarali ko'rinadi, chunki ular bir necha marta bosish orqali ma'nolar, talaffuzlar va sinonimlarni bir zumda qidirishlari mumkin.

Ikkinchi rasmda bir odam an'anaviy qog'oz lug'atda so'zlarni qidirmoqda. Ular kerakli narsani topish uchun sahifalarni jismonan varaqlab chiqmoqdalar. Ikkala rasm o'rtasidagi farq an'anaviy o'qish usullaridan zamonaviy raqamli yechimlarga o'tishni mukammal tarzda tasvirlaydi.

questions.prompt: What are the advantages of using an online dictionary?
questions.sampleA1: I like online dictionary. Easy. Find word fast.
questions.sampleA2: Online dictionary is good. I can find words easy and fast. And it's free. But sometimes the internet is slow.
questions.sampleB1: I think online dictionaries are very useful. For example, you can find words quickly. Also, they usually have the pronunciation. However, sometimes you need internet to use them.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the biggest advantage, to my mind, is speed — you can look up a word in a split second, which really comes in handy when you're reading. On top of that, most apps play the pronunciation out loud, so you pick up how words actually sound. And the thing is, they're constantly updated with new slang, so you're never behind the times.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga onlayn lug'at yoqadi. Oson. So'zni tez topish mumkin.
questions.uzSampleA2: Onlayn lug'at yaxshi. Men so'zlarni oson va tez topa olaman. Va u bepul. Lekin ba'zida internet sekin ishlaydi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, onlayn lug'atlar juda foydali.
Masalan, siz so'zlarni tezda topishingiz mumkin. Shuningdek, ularda odatda talaffuzi ham bo'ladi.
Biroq, ba'zan ulardan foydalanish uchun internet kerak bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Onlayn lug'atdan foydalanishning bir qancha afzalliklari bor.
Birinchidan, u an'anaviy kitobdan foydalanishdan ko'ra ancha tezroq. Siz so'zni tezda qidirib, uning ta'rifini topishingiz mumkin.
Ikkinchidan, ko'plab onlayn lug'atlar qo'shimcha xususiyatlarni taklif qiladi, masalan, misol gaplar va audio talaffuzlar.
Nihoyat, ular ko'pincha bepul va turli xil qurilmalarda osonlik bilan foydalanish mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the advantages of using an online dictionary?
sentenceStarters: "There are numerous advantages to using…" - "… dan foydalanishning ko'plab afzalliklari bor"
"Secondly, online dictionaries offer multimedia features that…" - "Ikkinchidan, onlayn lug'atlar … taqdim etadi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are numerous advantages to using an online dictionary over a physical one. Firstly, the speed and convenience are unmatched. You can find the definition of a word in a matter of milliseconds, which saves a considerable amount of time during reading or writing.
Secondly, online dictionaries offer multimedia features that paper dictionaries simply cannot provide. For instance, you can click an audio icon to hear the exact pronunciation of a word, which is incredibly helpful for language learners mastering spoken communication.
Finally, digital dictionaries are constantly updated with new words, slang, and idioms. Language is always evolving, and online platforms keep pace much faster than printed editions. As they say, "time is money," and the efficiency of digital tools makes them indispensable today.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Onlayn lug'atdan foydalanishning jismoniy lug'atga nisbatan ko'plab afzalliklari bor. Birinchidan, tezlik va qulaylik beqiyos. Siz so'zning ta'rifini millisekundlar ichida topishingiz mumkin, bu o'qish yoki yozish paytida sezilarli vaqtni tejaydi.

Ikkinchidan, onlayn lug'atlar qog'oz lug'atlar taqdim eta olmaydigan multimedia xususiyatlarini taklif qiladi. Misol uchun, so'zning aniq talaffuzini eshitish uchun audio belgisini bosishingiz mumkin, bu til o'rganuvchilar uchun og'zaki muloqotni o'zlashtirishda juda foydali.

Nihoyat, raqamli lug'atlar doimiy ravishda yangi so'zlar, jargonlar va iboralar bilan yangilanadi. Til doimo rivojlanib boradi va onlayn platformalar bosma nashrlarga qaraganda ancha tezroq rivojlanadi. Aytganlaridek, "vaqt - pul", va raqamli vositalarning samaradorligi ularni bugungi kunda ajralmas qiladi.

questions.prompt: Can using a paper dictionary help people remember words better?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I like paper. Paper good for words.
questions.sampleA2: I think yes. Because when I write the word, I remember it. And a paper dictionary is good because I can see many words.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think using a paper dictionary can be helpful. For example, when you look up a word, you see other words too. Also, I think it's better than a phone because you focus more. However, it takes more time.
questions.sampleB2: Yes, I'd say so, to be honest. When you thumb through a paper dictionary, the effort itself makes the word stick in your mind. I suppose it's because you're properly engaged rather than just skimming a screen. On top of that, you often stumble across nearby words, so you pick up extra vocabulary almost by accident. It's slower, but the learning tends to run deeper.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Menga qog'oz yoqadi. Qog'oz so'zlar uchun yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, ha. Chunki men so'zni yozganimda, uni eslab qolaman. Va qog'oz lug'at yaxshi, chunki men ko'p so'zlarni ko'rishim mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha, qog'oz lug'atdan foydalanish foydali bo'lishi mumkin.
Masalan, bir so'zni qidirganingizda, boshqa so'zlarni ham ko'rasiz.
Shuningdek, menimcha, bu telefondan yaxshiroq, chunki siz ko'proq diqqat qaratasiz.
Biroq, bu ko'proq vaqt talab qiladi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Menimcha, qog'oz lug'atlar so'zlarni yaxshiroq eslab qolishga yordam berishi haqida yaxshi bahs qilish mumkin. Sahifalarni jismonan qidirishning o'zi sizni til bilan faolroq shug'ullanishga majbur qiladi. Siz shunchaki onlayn lug'at bilan bo'lganingiz kabi passiv ravishda ma'lumot olmayapsiz. Faol ravishda qidirayotganingiz va shug'ullanayotganingiz sababli, bu ko'proq esda qoladi.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Can using a paper dictionary help people remember words better?
idioms: slow and steady wins the race - "sekin va sabotli poygada yutadi"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I strongly believe that using a paper dictionary…" - "Ha, qog'oz lug'atdan foydalanish … ga ishonaman"
"When you use a physical book, the process is…" - "Jismoniy kitobdan foydalanganingizda, jarayon…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I strongly believe that using a paper dictionary can actually aid in memory retention. When you use a physical book, the process is inherently slower. You have to think about alphabetical order, scan the page, and actively search for the word. This extra effort and cognitive engagement often make the word stick in your mind longer.
Moreover, while scanning a page, you often stumble upon other interesting words nearby. This accidental learning broadens your vocabulary in a way that typing a single word into a search bar does not.
Furthermore, using a physical book provides a tactile experience that many people find less distracting than looking at a screen filled with notifications. While digital tools are faster, the "slow and steady" approach of a paper dictionary often leads to deeper learning.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men qog'oz lug'atdan foydalanish xotirani saqlashga yordam berishiga qattiq ishonaman. Jismoniy kitobdan foydalanganda, jarayon sekinroq bo'ladi. Siz alifbo tartibi haqida o'ylashingiz, sahifani ko'rib chiqishingiz va so'zni faol ravishda qidirishingiz kerak. Bu qo'shimcha harakat va kognitiv jalb qilish ko'pincha so'zni xotirangizda uzoqroq saqlaydi.

Bundan tashqari, sahifani ko'rib chiqayotganda, siz ko'pincha yaqin atrofdagi boshqa qiziqarli so'zlarga duch kelasiz. Bu tasodifiy o'rganish sizning lug'at boyligingizni bitta so'zni qidiruv satriga kiritishdan ko'ra kengaytiradi.

Bundan tashqari, jismoniy kitobdan foydalanish ko'pchilik uchun ekranda bildirishnomalar bilan to'ldirilgan ekranga qarashdan ko'ra kamroq chalg'itadigan taktil tajribani taqdim etadi. Raqamli vositalar tezroq bo'lsa-da, qog'oz lug'atning "sekin va barqaror" yondashuvi ko'pincha chuqurroq o'rganishga olib keladi.

questions.prompt: Share a time when you visited a historical or cultural site.
questions.sampleA1: I go to museum. It is old. I see many things. It is good.
questions.sampleA2: I went to a castle last year. It was very big and old. I saw many rooms and a big tower. I liked it because it was interesting to see how people lived before.
questions.sampleB1: I remember visiting the Colosseum in Rome. It was really impressive to see how big it was. I think it's important to visit places like that because you can learn about the past. For example, I learned about gladiators and Roman history. It was also very crowded, however.
questions.sampleB2: Right, I'd like to tell you about the time I visited Registan Square in Samarkand a couple of years back. To be honest, I'd seen countless photos of it, but nothing quite prepared me for the real thing. The moment I set foot on the square, I was blown away by the three towering madrasahs, all covered in these intricate turquoise tiles that seemed to glow in the sunlight. I spent hours just wandering around, soaking up the atmosphere, and I remember taking far too many photos to capture every angle. As for how it made me feel — honestly, it was quite humbling. Standing in a place where scholars and merchants had crossed paths centuries ago gave me goosebumps. I suppose it made me realise how small we are in the grand scheme of things. There was this overwhelming sense of history in the air, and I felt genuinely proud of my country's rich cultural heritage. As for the bigger question, I firmly believe that visiting historical sites helps us understand the past far better than any textbook could. The thing is, reading about something is one thing, but actually being there really brings history to life. When you can touch the walls and picture how people lived, it strikes a chord in a way facts and dates simply can't. It builds a kind of empathy for previous generations, and it passes on a sense of identity. At the end of the day, if we want to know where we're heading, we've got to understand where we've come from.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men muzeyga boraman. U eski. Men ko'p narsalarni ko'raman. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men o'tgan yili bir qasrga bordim. U juda katta va eski edi. Men ko'p xonalarni va katta minorani ko'rdim. Menga yoqdi, chunki odamlar ilgari qanday yashaganini ko'rish qiziqarli edi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Esimda, Rimdagi Kolizeyga borganman. Uning naqadar katta ekanligini ko'rish juda ta'sirli edi. Menimcha, shunga o'xshash joylarga borish muhim, chunki o'tmish haqida bilib olishingiz mumkin.
Masalan, men gladiatorlar va Rim tarixi haqida bilib oldim. Biroq, u yer juda gavjum ham edi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Bir marta Yaponiyaning Kioto shahriga borish va Fushimi Inari ibodatxonasini o'rganish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lganman. Tog'ga o'ralashib boruvchi yorqin qizil torii darvozalarining cheksiz yo'li chindan ham hayratlanarli edi. Bu menga Shinto e'tiqodlari va umuman olganda yapon madaniyatini chuqurroq anglash imkoniyatini berdi. Menimcha, tarixiy joylarni bevosita his qilish, ular haqida shunchaki o'qishdan ko'ra, turli madaniyatlarni boyroq tushunishni ta'minlaydi. Shintoizm haqida bilish bir narsa, lekin uning vizual ifodasiga sho'ng'ish butunlay boshqa narsa. Bu asrlar davomida saqlanib qolgan an'anaga aloqadorlik hissini uyg'otdi.

vocabulary.title: Q7 - Share a time when you visited a historical or cultural site
sentenceStarters: "I'd like to share an experience from last spring when…" - "Men o'tgan bahordagi bo'lgan voqeani aytib bermoqchiman…"
"Standing in the middle of such a historic location made me feel…" - "Bunday tarixiy joyning o'rtasida turish menga … his qildirdi"

bulletPoints: Share a time when you visited a historical or cultural site.
How did being there make you feel?
How can visiting historical places help people understand the past better?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A time I visited a historical site:
I'd like to share an experience from last spring when I visited the ancient city of Samarkand. Walking through the Registan Square, surrounded by the majestic madrasahs covered in intricate blue tiles, was an absolutely unforgettable experience. The sheer scale and architectural brilliance of the place were mesmerizing.
How being there made me feel:
Standing in the middle of such a historic location made me feel deeply humbled. It was like stepping back in time. I felt a profound sense of connection to the generations of scholars and merchants who had walked those exact same paths centuries ago. It was a powerful reminder of our rich cultural heritage and how fleeting our own time here really is.
How visiting historical places helps people understand the past:
I believe visiting historical sites is crucial for understanding the past because it brings history to life in a way that textbooks simply cannot. When you physically stand where history happened, you gain a tangible sense of the scale and reality of those events. It fosters empathy and respect for the struggles and achievements of our ancestors. As the saying goes, "to know your future, you must know your past."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Tarixiy joyga tashrif buyurganim haqida:

O'tgan bahorda Samarqand qadimiy shahriga tashrif buyurganim haqidagi tajribamni baham ko'rmoqchiman. Registon maydonida sayr qilib, murakkab ko'k rangli koshinlar bilan qoplangan ulug'vor madrasalar bilan o'ralganim mutlaqo unutilmas tajriba bo'ldi. Bu joyning ulkanligi va me'moriy mahorati meni sehrlab qo'ydi.

U yerda bo'lish menga qanday ta'sir qildi:

Bunday tarixiy joyning o'rtasida turish meni juda kamtar his qildirdi. Go'yo vaqt orqaga qaytgandek bo'ldim. Asrlar oldin xuddi shu yo'llardan yurgan olimlar va savdogarlar avlodlariga chuqur aloqadorlik hissini tuygandek bo'ldim. Bu bizning boy madaniy merosimiz va bu yerdagi o'z vaqtimiz qanchalik o'tkinchi ekanligining kuchli eslatmasi edi.

Tarixiy joylarga tashrif buyurish odamlarga o'tmishni tushunishga qanday yordam beradi:

Menimcha, tarixiy joylarga tashrif buyurish o'tmishni tushunish uchun juda muhim, chunki u tarixni darsliklar qila olmaydigan tarzda jonlantiradi. Tarix sodir bo'lgan joyda jismonan turganda, siz o'sha voqealarning ko'lami va haqiqatiga aniq his qilasiz. Bu ajdodlarimizning kurashlari va yutuqlariga nisbatan hamdardlik va hurmatni oshiradi. Maqolda aytilganidek, "kelajagingni bilmoqchi bo'lsang, o'tmishingni bilishing kerak".

questions.sampleB2: Right, the idea that schools should start later in the day is one that really divides opinion. On the one hand, I can definitely see where the supporters are coming from. Teenagers are notoriously bad at getting up early, and their body clocks are simply wired differently. If schools pushed back the start time by an hour or so, students would turn up better rested, which would almost certainly boost concentration and grades, since a well-rested brain absorbs information far more easily. On top of that, it would take the pressure off those chaotic mornings, so everyone would be far less stressed. On the other hand, though, there are some real practical hurdles. The thing is, most parents have to set off for work early, so a later start could throw childcare into chaos. It would also eat into the time for after-school clubs, sports and part-time jobs, and the school buses might end up caught up in rush-hour traffic. So it's by no means a straightforward change. There's clearly a lot to weigh up. Personally, though, I come down on the side of a later start. To my mind, the wellbeing of students has to come first, because a tired, half-asleep class simply won't learn properly, no matter how early they arrive. Sure, the logistics would need ironing out, but with a bit of planning I honestly think it's well worth a try. After all, health is wealth, and rested students are happier and more productive, so in the long run, everybody stands to benefit.

vocabulary.title: Q8 - Schools should start later in the day
idioms: burning the candle at both ends - "haddan tashqari ko'p ishlash (charchash)"
sentenceStarters: "The question of whether schools should start later…" - "Maktablar keyinroq boshlanishi kerakmi degan savol…"
"Proponents of later start times argue that…" - "Kechroq boshlash tarafdorlari … deb ta'kidlaydi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
The question of whether schools should start later in the day is hotly debated among educators and parents. Proponents of later start times argue that it significantly aligns with the natural sleep patterns of adolescents. Better sleep leads directly to improved focus and productivity in the classroom. Furthermore, a later start reduces the frantic morning rush, which lowers stress levels for both students and their families before the day even begins.
Conversely, opponents point out several practical challenges. A major issue is that later school times severely disrupt parents’ work schedules, creating childcare issues in the morning. Additionally, pushing the school day back inevitably shortens the available time for after-school activities, sports, and part-time jobs. There can also be serious transportation challenges, as school bus schedules might clash with peak rush hour traffic.
Personally, I believe that while the logistical challenges are real, the health and academic benefits of well-rested students should take priority. As the saying goes, "health is wealth" — if students are exhausted, the quality of their education suffers, making the early start counterproductive.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Maktablar kun davomida kechroq boshlanishi kerakmi degan savol pedagoglar va ota-onalar o'rtasida qizg'in muhokama qilinmoqda. Kechroq boshlash vaqtlarini yoqlovchilarning ta'kidlashicha, bu o'smirlarning tabiiy uyqu tartibiga sezilarli darajada mos keladi. Yaxshiroq uyqu bevosita sinfda diqqatni jamlash va unumdorlikni oshiradi. Bundan tashqari, kechroq boshlash ertalabki vahimali shoshilishni kamaytiradi, bu esa kun boshlanishidan oldin o'quvchilar va ularning oilalari uchun stress darajasini pasaytiradi.

Aksincha, qarshilar bir nechta amaliy muammolarni ko'rsatmoqda. Asosiy muammo shundaki, maktab vaqtlarining kechiktirilishi ota-onalarning ish jadvalini keskin buzadi va ertalab bolalarni parvarish qilish muammolarini yaratadi. Bundan tashqari, o'quv kunini orqaga surish, albatta, darsdan keyingi mashg'ulotlar, sport va yarim kunlik ishlar uchun mavjud vaqtni qisqartiradi. Maktab avtobuslari jadvali tirbandlikning eng yuqori soatlariga to'g'ri kelishi mumkinligi sababli, transport bilan bog'liq jiddiy muammolar ham bo'lishi mumkin.

Shaxsan men, logistika bilan bog'liq muammolar haqiqiy bo'lsa-da, yaxshi dam olgan o'quvchilarning salomatligi va o'quv yutuqlari ustuvor bo'lishi kerak, deb hisoblayman. Aytishlaricha, "sog'lik - boylik" - agar o'quvchilar charchagan bo'lsa, ularning ta'lim sifati yomonlashadi va erta boshlash samarasiz bo'ladi.
